title: Surge tail-amplification in multimodal microbatching due to kernel-autoselect regression
creator: Linh Tran
description: Multiple customers (notably NovaHealth and LedgerSoft on Private clusters in eu-west) reported sudden TTFT regressions and tokens/sec collapse during mixed-text+image workloads. The condition surfaced after a GPU driver and runtime kernel heuristic change rolled to runtime-1.19: one-path microbatch interleaving triggers an autoselect path that chooses a fallback GEMM kernel for certain attention sizes, amplifying tail latency under tail-heavy request mixes. This ticket tracks the investigation, immediate customer mitigations, and a short-lived hotfix to pin kernel selection heuristic and add a per-tenant microbatch gate.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy rw-mix-14b-v1 on a PRV eu-west cluster with runtime-1.19 and recent driver stack
2) Send burst of 1000 mixed requests over 60s consisting of: 60% short-text (<=64 tokens), 30% long-text (>=1024 tokens), 10% image-augmented prompts (multimodal with 128 token captions)
3) Observe TTFT metric in Console: median unaffected, p95/p99 spikes by 2.5-6x; tokens/sec per-worker drops by ~40% for 20-40s windows
4) Correlate with kernel-selection telemetry: switches from fast fused-attention path to fallback GEMM for ~30% of microbatches
investigation_notes: Telemetry: kernel_selector logs show increased 'fallback_reason=unsupported_tile' events after driver bump; occurrences align with tail-latency windows
KV-cache: eviction churn increases when image-augmented requests interleave with long-text sessions, causing more frequent cache misses but not sufficient alone to explain tokens/sec collapse
Prefetching: existing warmup reduces steady-state latency but cannot prevent the transient kernel-autoselect oscillation under bursty mixes
Network: VPC egress and NLB metrics show no packet loss or queuing correlated to the windows; root is within the GPU runtime/kernel decision path

Customer traces: NovaHealth provided an incident trace showing back-to-back microbatches where kernel_selection toggled between fused-attn and gemm, introducing 6-12ms additional per-token cost in affected windows
fix_summary: 1) Short-term hotfix: patch kernel-selector to pin preferred fused-attention kernels for known attention shapes used by rw-mix-14b-v1 and disable the new 'tile-autoselect' heuristic for runtime-1.19 on Private/Dedicated. 2) Add per-tenant microbatch gate to avoid interleaving multimodal microbatches that cause shape heterogeneity on the same worker. 3) Instrument an emergency metric and alert (p99-TTFT delta > 2x baseline) and an automated rollback flag for runtime rollout.
rollout_plan: Canary: apply kernel-selector pin to 3 eu-west private nodes for NovaHealth and LedgerSoft (hour 0-2)
Validation: run synthetic multimodal burst harness for 30m; verify p95/p99 TTFT within 20% of pre-regression baseline
Gradual: expand patch to remaining eu-west private nodes and Dedicated pool over next 4 hours if stable
Fallback: retain capability to flip runtime-1.19 'autoselect' flag cluster-wide within 10 minutes via orchestration control plane
Postmortem: collect full traces and produce a customer-facing incident summary within 72 hours
comments: 2026-03-10 Miguel Santos: initial triage — reproduced locally with the burst harness; kernel_selector fallback events spike when multimodal microbatches interleave. Allocated a hotfix branch.
2026-03-11 Aisha Patel (SRE): canary nodes deployed; observed immediate drop in p99 TTFT on canary hosts. Preparing rollback play if we see regressions elsewhere.
2026-03-11 Linh Tran: patched kernel-selector heuristic to treat 'unsupported_tile' as non-fatal and keep fused-attn path for known shapes. Added toggle flag in runtime config.

2026-03-12 Miguel Santos: microbatch-gating introduced — new gate prevents scheduling of heterogeneous microbatches on the same worker for 30s windows. Initial tests show tokens/sec restored to ~95% of baseline under synthetic load.
2026-03-12 Customer update sent to NovaHealth and LedgerSoft with measures taken and expected next steps. They confirmed improved behavior on their private clusters after the canary patch.
